annotations.title: utilpeek: list the occurrences of a recurrence rule (RRULE) in a time zone

description: utilpeek: Expand an iCalendar RRULE into dates. For cron use cron_next_runs; to build an event use build_ics_event. Returns an RFC 5545 RRULE and a start expanded into its occurrence list with python-dateutil in an IANA time zone: wall-clock times keep across DST changes. Up to 1,000 occurrences, an optional [from, to] window, extra until and exdates. Returns ISO 8601 times with offset and whether more exist. Pure computation: no network access, nothing stored. The search stops at search_horizon (1 hour for SECONDLY up to 100 years for YEARLY) and after 1.5 s. A bad rule, a rule that never matches (Feb 31) or a bad date or zone is a 422 (not charged). Typically under 0.1 s. Price: USD 0.001. Free: 10 utilpeek calls per IP per UTC day. Docs: https://tanod.dev/learn/ics-calendar-api.html

rrule.description: RFC 5545 RRULE, with or without the RRULE: prefix.
